en.title: The superlative
en.summary: The superlative says that one thing has the most of a quality in a group.

paragraphs: We use the superlative to say that one thing or person is first in a group of three or more: the highest, the best, the most useful. We almost always put the before it. We name the group with in or of.

items: Everest is **the highest** mountain in the world.
She is **the cleverest** student in the class.
This is **the most useful** tool of all.
It was **the worst** day of my life.

paragraphs: Short adjectives add -est and long adjectives take most. The spelling rules are the same as for the comparative: a final e adds only st, a single consonant after a short vowel is doubled, and y changes to iest.
Use in with a place or a group of people: the tallest girl in the class, the longest river in Europe. Use of with a plural noun or a number: the best of the three, the oldest of my friends.
The superlative is often followed by a present perfect and ever: It is the best film I have ever seen. The word the can be dropped after a possessive, as in my best friend.

items: Wrong: **Tom is tallest boy.** Right: **Tom is the tallest boy.**
Wrong: **the oldest from my friends** Right: **the oldest of my friends**

ro.title: Superlativul
ro.summary: Superlativul arată că o ființă sau un lucru are o însușire la cel mai înalt grad.

paragraphs: Superlativul arată că un element se află pe primul loc într-un grup. El exprimă gradul maxim al unei calități atunci când comparăm un element cu toate celelalte.
În limba română folosim formele „cel mai”, „cea mai”, „cei mai” sau „cele mai”. Alegem forma potrivită în funcție de genul și numărul substantivului, urmată de adjectiv.
